correctness.rationale: For monotone maps preserving zero, nilpotence is equivalent to f(x)<x at every positive x. Deleting letters from a composition word can only increase its output, since each generator is bounded above by the identity and all are monotone. A length-N word has at least a_i occurrences of some i, so it is bounded by f_i^a_i=0. Distributivity on a chain identifies each join power with the maximum of all words of that length; strict descent gives the separate n bound. At n=N, equality forces the full consecutive descent. At every x>=2 a map taking x to x-1 contributes a jump in its hitting-time height, whose increments are 0 or 1 by monotonicity and strict descent. The total height jumps are exactly N-1, so there is exactly one label per position. At its jump x the label's image is x-1; on a plateau the previous jump fixes the image by monotonicity below and the required height of the image above. Conversely taking the last position in the preceding height level yields precisely the desired image and actual heights by induction. This verifies both sides of the bijection, the index-one and k=1 cases, and constant extension past N. The uploaded enumerator is bounded corroboration, not the proof used here.
residual_risks: The census is only for C_N; no larger-chain enumeration or general-semiring assertion is certified.

The coloring is an explicit inverse construction and a complete rigidity result, distinguishing the equality tuples from a large background of individual Catalan-counted maps.
